title: Migration from SnappyData/Spark to Amazon Redshift Serverless
subtitle: Replacing an unmaintained in-memory Spark analytics cluster with Amazon Redshift Serverless and Metabase for cost-effective 10M+ row analytical querying.
overview: When our legacy SnappyData (Spark-based in-memory analytics engine) reached end-of-life and created continuous operational instability, we migrated our analytics foundation to Amazon Redshift Serverless. This migration streamlined our ETL pipelines, restored full ANSI SQL compliance for business analysts, and drastically reduced operational overhead while querying over 10.8 million transaction records through Metabase.
problem: SnappyData became abandonware, leaving us without critical security updates. Furthermore, Spark SQL lacked complete ANSI SQL support, complicating reporting queries. The manual memory management and cluster node maintenance imposed severe operational burdens during heavy batch analytics cycles.

implementation.title: 1. Redshift Serverless Cluster Provisioning & Cost Tuning
implementation.description: Created the Redshift Serverless workgroup and namespace. Crucially, tuned the base capacity down from the expensive 128 RPU default to 4 RPU to keep costs minimal during development and light batch loads.
implementation.code:
-- Provisioning parameters:
-- Base Capacity: 4 RPU (Redshift Processing Units)
-- Network: VPC security group with inbound port 5439 restricted to BI service CIDR
-- Public Access: Enabled with IAM role credential enforcement

implementation.title: 2. Analytics Schema Definition
implementation.description: Designed high-throughput target tables in Redshift utilizing optimal data types for financial transactions and patient demographic breakdowns.
implementation.code:
CREATE TABLE dev.public.transaction_items (
    id VARCHAR NOT NULL,
    system VARCHAR NOT NULL,
    transactionId VARCHAR NOT NULL,
    itemDescription VARCHAR(2500),
    itemChargingType VARCHAR,
    itemAmount DECIMAL(16,2),
    patientGender VARCHAR,
    patientDateOfBirth DATE,
    patientLanguage VARCHAR,
    patientMobileContactNumber VARCHAR
);

implementation.title: 3. Shell Data Cleaning for Strict Redshift COPY Requirements
implementation.description: Sanitized delimiter quotation artifacts and rectified millisecond timestamps (which require period notation `HH:MM:SS.sss` rather than colon notation) using regular expression streaming transformations.
implementation.code:
# 1. Fix broken quoted pipe delimiters
sed -E 's/"([|]|\s*$)/\1/g' transaction_items.csv > transaction_items_cleaned.csv

# 2. Fix millisecond timestamp format from HH:MM:SS:sss to HH:MM:SS.sss
sed -E 's/([0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}):([0-9]{3})/\1.\2/g' \
    transaction_items-1753471509266.csv > transaction_items.csv

implementation.title: 4. High-Speed S3 COPY Ingestion & Error Verification
implementation.description: Loaded the cleansed files from S3 using Redshift's massively parallel COPY command with IAM role authentication, verifying integrity via the sys_load_error_detail system view.
implementation.code:
COPY dev.public.transaction_items 
FROM 's3://arogya-analytics/transactions-items/transaction_items_cleaned3.csv'
IAM_ROLE 'arn:aws:iam::143489828581:role/service-role/AmazonRedshift-CommandsAccessRole-20250726T052415'
FORMAT AS CSV 
DELIMITER '|' 
IGNOREHEADER 1 
REGION AS 'ap-southeast-1';

-- Verify any ingestion warnings or failed rows:
SELECT * 
FROM sys_load_error_detail 
ORDER BY start_time DESC;

implementation.title: 5. Metabase OSS Docker Deployment & Connection
implementation.description: Deployed Metabase via Docker and configured the Redshift JDBC connector for SQL reporting and visualization.
implementation.code:
docker run -d -p 3001:3000 \
  -v ~/metabase-data:/metabase-data \
  -e "MB_DB_FILE=/metabase-data/metabase.db" \
  --name metabase metabase/metabase:latest

# Connect Metabase to dev.public.transaction_items on port 5439 with SSL enabled

impact: Successfully ingested over 10.8 million transaction rows with zero data loss or partition truncation.
Eliminated custom cluster provisioning and maintenance outages by leveraging serverless auto-scaling.
Empowered product and financial teams to write standard ANSI SQL queries and build self-service Metabase dashboards.
lessons: Redshift's default base capacity of 128 RPU can cause massive cost spikes if left untouched; always evaluate workload scale and throttle base capacity down to 4 or 8 RPU for modest workloads.
Redshift's COPY command is strict about timestamp millisecond syntax — preprocessing delimiters and timestamps in S3 saves hours of debugging load failures.
